propositions: A seeded-defect mutant corpus (e2_mutant_corpus.jsonl) was deterministically constructed from real cleanly-closed plans for five defect classes to provide known-ground-truth labels for gate detection power measurement.

Pure counting helpers (e2_counting.py: classify_pair, run_validity) and golden tests were built offline to determine PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE verdicts with a ≥0.20 INDETERMINATE run-validity cap, independent of LLM evaluation.

The benchmark harness (run_e2_benchmark.py) implements store isolation via standalone git clone with its own .git directory to prevent mutation commits from contaminating the production tickets tracker.

The expensive ~100-run LLM batch baseline (live gate sweep over mutant corpus) was permanently rejected on cost grounds and is superseded by the standing criterion_effectiveness.py recorder on main (change #798) which accumulates detection/FP signal at zero marginal LLM cost from production reviews.

The deterministic half (corpus, thresholds, harness seams, counting helpers, golden tests) was designed and built as WIP on branch calib/6982-e2 but intentionally not landed on main because the harness only exists to drive the rejected batch.
History-based baseline mining is dead due to insufficient plan-v3 sidecar baselines (~4 vs ~200 needed after impact_model_version bump stranded the history.
